subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: Finex latency & streaming reqs
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: Finex latency & streaming reqs

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and the items we agreed to confirm: 

- SLOs you called out: p95 first-byte latency target ~250ms for interactive streaming flows; p99 target as a fall-back objective (<= 800ms).
- Typical request profile: interactive chat with streaming enabled (UI consumes tokens as they arrive).
- Average request size estimate from the call: 180 tokens in (prompt + context) and 60 tokens generated on average.
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~3k tokens/sec (aggregate across users).
- Peak burst expectations: up to ~12k tokens/sec during campaign spikes; concurrency spikes ~120 simultaneous streams.

Next steps from our side:
1) We'll run a throughput plan and back-of-envelope capacity calculation for your stated steady vs peak token/sec and concurrency numbers.
2) Please share a sample traffic export (anonymized) with distribution of tokens per request, request QPS by hour, and percentiles for sequence lengths — that will let us recommend batching/quantization/memory footprint.
3) If you have hard latency SLAs per region or for specific endpoints (e.g., search vs chat), flag them so we can model routing/fallback.

I'll attach a starter throughput calc (simple workbook) and follow up with recommended Dedicated config and expected token-unit costs for both steady and burst modes.

Thanks — Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: redwood_throughput_calc_v1.xlsx (workbook stub with sheets: assumptions, steady_vs_peak, cost_estimates)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finex.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up: Finex latency & streaming reqs

Rafael —

Appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from Priya and me after sync with our infra team: 

- The p95 250ms is for the "typing" use case (first-token), but for overall 95th-token latency we target <= 500ms. The p99 objective is more flexible but we'd like it under 1.2s if possible.
- Our current front-end consumes streamed tokens at ~70 tokens/sec per active connection. We approximate 40 tokens/sec sustained is normal, 70 tokens/sec when users are in rapid typing/auto-complete mode.
- Average tokens per response: 60 is accurate; 95th percentile responses can go to ~400 tokens (long-form generation).
- Steady-state user base in US-east: ~250 active streaming sessions during business hours. Peak promo/test events have hit ~1.2k concurrent sessions historically.

We'll attach a small sample traffic extract (anonymized) showing QPS and token distributions; Priya will send that. Priya — ping if you want us to redact more fields.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Turner
Senior Product Manager, Finex
alex.turner@finex.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up: Finex latency & streaming reqs

Alex/Priya —

Great, that helps. A few follow-ups so we can size properly: 

1) Can you confirm hourly QPS distribution (or approximate %) between: baseline hours, peak hour(s), and weekend traffic? We model batching and autoscale differently if peak is sustained vs short bursts.
2) Please provide the token-length percentile table you mentioned (p50/p90/p95/p99) for both prompt+context and generated tokens. Long tail (p99) at 400 tokens will materially change memory and batch size choices.
3) Do you require regional routing (multi-region active-active) or is US-east-only sufficient at first?
4) Streaming specifics: is client-side RTT typically 30–50ms (we'll need this for first-byte latency calc) and do you need guaranteed ordering across multiple calls per user?

We'll take the sample and run two configurations: a) cost-optimized (quantization + larger batching, slightly higher tail latencies), b) latency-optimized (smaller batches, lower quantization, more capacity) and provide estimated token/sec capacity and expected p95/p99 tail latencies under both.

I'll target sending the calc + recommended Dedicated pod sizes by EOD tomorrow once we get your sample.

— Rafael

From: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finex.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up: Finex latency & streaming reqs

Rafael —

Attaching the anonymized sample we talked about. Key numbers pulled from last 30 days: 

- Avg QPS (US-east steady hours): 12 QPS (requests/sec) -> ~3,000 tokens/sec steady (given avg tokens/request ~250 total).
- Peak QPS (promo spikes): 48 QPS -> ~12,000 tokens/sec.
- Average concurrent streaming sessions (steady): 250; peak concurrent: 1,200.
- Token length percentiles (response gen): p50=60, p90=180, p95=300, p99=420.
- Client RTT median: ~45ms; 95th RTT ~120ms.
- Region: US-east primarily; may expand to EU in Q4.

Files attached: finex_traffic_sample.csv (anonymized columns: timestamp,qps,tokens_per_request,p95_response_tokens)

Let us know if you need a longer history or raw logs. We can also provide a short job to replay traffic if helpful.

Thanks — Priya
